findings.claim: 1. Rows H16, H17, H18. Node `cut` takes `branch` from pin's predicted name and drops the tree's real branch: "branch, base and uncommitted from $pin.output, the rest from $tree.output". The tree run's `handoff` (:168, "branch from git branch --show-current") and gauntlet-design.md:155 `paths` read the branch from git, and the mend rebases that one. No node checks that the two names match, though Homes :194 says "the tree run reads it from git".
findings.failure_scenario: Archon's naming changes, or pin's `norm` differs from Archon's on some WORKFLOW_ID. Archon finds no local branch with its own name and cuts the tree from origin/<baseBranch>, a start point :195 forbids, and nothing notices. Writing and the mend commit on the real branch. Landing gets pin's empty branch at base (gauntlet-design.md:82). Its `onto` sees an ancestor, `merge --ff-only` does nothing and the run reports `landed`. `archon complete <pin branch>` then targets the wrong branch and the work never reaches the checkout.

findings.claim: 2. Rows H20 and P8. Node `baseline` runs the full `GAUNTLET_TEST_COMMAND` (up to 900 s, in the foreground) into `gauntlet/baseline/<slug>.txt`, but no node in any design reads that file. Red uses only the brief baseline (writing-design.md:30, :145; landing-design.md:16). writing-design.md:14 calls the full file "unparsed, with no per-test listing" and :526 forbids the test writer from reaching it. It travels only as a required pass-through field (gauntlet-design.md:163, :222). This is a node the sequence does not need (CLAUDE.md 1.3).
findings.failure_scenario: On every run, the tree run's first phase holds a full test-suite run of up to 15 minutes on the production host. It runs beside copy-in and before writing can start. Its output is never compared, shown or parsed, so the run pays the time and CPU for nothing.

findings.claim: 3. Row A27 (this design's text, not the verdict). The node timeout depends on the repository's env: "timeout: <GAUNTLET_TEST_TIMEOUT plus 60 s, in ms; 960000 when unset>". The documented `timeout` is a fixed ms value in YAML (workflow-language.md:93), with no env expansion. The bash body already bounds the command with `timeout -k 10 "${GAUNTLET_TEST_TIMEOUT:-900}"`. The same form is copied at writing-design.md:399 and landing-design.md:61, :79, :146.
findings.failure_scenario: The builder can only write a literal, which in practice means 960000. A repository sets GAUNTLET_TEST_TIMEOUT: "1800" and its suite takes 1200 s. Archon kills `baseline` at 960 s and the tree run fails, though the repository's own limit was not reached. That is a stop over a technicality (1.4). Omitting the node timeout loses nothing, because the inner `timeout -k` already bounds the process.

findings.claim: 4. Rows P11 and H20. The cut accepts a repository with no test command and carries on: "GAUNTLET_TEST_COMMAND unset or blank: write the file with the one line \"no test command\"". Writing requires the command: writing-design.md:512 says "Writing needs GAUNTLET_TEST_COMMAND and GAUNTLET_TEST_BRIEF_COMMAND to be set", and :107 says "blank: every mode exits 1 naming it". landing-design.md:62 also exits 1 on a blank brief command, while writing-design.md:502 writes "no test command" for it.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository with no GAUNTLET_TEST_COMMAND runs intake, plan review, spec review, the cut and the baseline, all paid in agent tokens and owner pauses. The baseline records "no test command" as success. Only then does stage.py exit 1 inside writing. The run stops on a condition known before the cut, and the cut's tolerant branch only delays that stop (1.3).

findings.claim: 5. Row H20 (also P8). The Homes row forbids "any other baseline file" for "The test baseline | gauntlet/baseline/<slug>.txt of the tree, written once by node baseline". writing-design.md:502 makes the same node also write `gauntlet/baseline/<slug>.brief.txt`. That is the file red is judged against (writing-design.md:30; landing-design.md:40, :64), and gauntlet-design.md:156, :194 depend on it.
findings.failure_scenario: A builder or checker enforcing worktree-cut's Homes table rejects writing:step 8's brief file, the only baseline any red check reads. If they follow writing-design.md instead, the cut design's home rule is broken. The design never gives the brief file a home, so one of the two documents is wrong.

findings.claim: 6. Rows H16 and H17. `uncommitted` is computed and handed off, but no node reads it: "Node pin lists the changed tracked paths in uncommitted, the cut hands them off, and the run goes on." The only readers of `$cut.output` (gauntlet-design.md:80-88) take outcome, worktree, branch, line and verdict. `base` is unread the same way. Line 9's reason, "because the plan and spec were reviewed against that code", is false when uncommitted edits exist. The plan and spec agents read the live working tree (FENCE_READ=., gauntlet-design.md:31), and untracked new files are not listed at all (:69, "tracked paths").
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has uncommitted edits, or untracked new files, that the plan relies on. The reviewers read them in the checkout. The tree is cut from HEAD without them, and writing builds against code the plan was not reviewed on. The `uncommitted` list that would explain this reaches no node and no owner gate.

findings.claim: 7. Rows H9 and H16. The `tree` node's required input `checkout` has no source: "with: { checkout: <the checkout's absolute root>, ...". pin's output (:66-69, :105) carries no checkout field. The documented standard variables ($WORKFLOW_ID, $ARTIFACTS_DIR, $BASE_BRANCH, ...) include no checkout path. gauntlet-design.md:156, :169 and landing's mend still depend on `checkout` through `paths`.
findings.failure_scenario: workflow-builder reaches step 3 with no expression to bind. A guessed literal or a missing binding gives copy-in (:153, a path relative to $INPUTS.checkout) and the mend's `git -C $INPUTS.checkout` a wrong or empty root. copy-in then fails or copies nothing. The fix is for pin to print the checkout root.

findings.claim: 8. Internal (also row H7). copy-in silently skips a plan or spec that its input names but the checkout lacks: "each present in the checkout ... target absent: cp -n" (also :48, "each only when present there"). handoff (:168-170) still prints a tree path for any non-empty input.
findings.failure_scenario: The plan input is non-empty, but gauntlet/plans/approved/<slug>.txt was moved or deleted in the checkout after plan review. copy-in copies nothing and exits 0. handoff hands writing a path to a file that does not exist, and writing's agents work with no plan instead of the run failing at the cut.

findings.claim: 9. Row H23, and the 'Removing the tree and its branch' home at gauntlet-design.md:354, which has no contracts row. Homes forbids "any write in the tree by a gauntlet-run node". Landing, a gauntlet-run block, removes the tree with `archon complete $INPUTS.branch --force` (landing-design.md:262; gauntlet-design.md:354). gauntlet-design.md:343 forbids only "a rebase, test run or commit in the tree from gauntlet-run", the narrower rule.
findings.failure_scenario: A checker applying this design's Homes table to land/land.yaml flags `remove`, the documented home for removing the tree. The two designs give different forbidden sets for the same concern.
